Adjusted view using SLOOS insights:
- The FOMC statement is dovish and supportive (zero rates, strong QE, average inflation targeting, and readiness to adjust).
- SLOOS (Q3 2020) indicates banks broadly tightened standards and saw weaker demand in C&I and CRE loans; forbearance policies and capital positions influenced lending practices. Consumer credit—especially subprime—was soft, while demand was strong for GSE-eligible and QM non-jumbo mortgages, which comprise most bank mortgage originations.
- This mix means policy support is aligning with the strongest segment (agency MBS/mortgages), but credit availability for businesses and riskier consumers remains constrained, dampening the recovery impulse despite accommodative financial conditions.

Net: relative to the prior assessment, SLOOS tilts the outlook slightly more negative due to tighter bank lending and weaker non-mortgage loan demand, partially offset by robust agency-eligible mortgage demand and Fed support.
